projects.projectName: Premera Blue Cross - Producer Portal Development - Phase 1

riskDescription.context: The SOW term ended on August 31, 2026, but the project continued through Production deployment completed by October 23, 2026, creating a 53-day overrun with no contract amendment documented. (ART - Work Assignment; ALT - Watchlist Summary)
riskDescription.condition: If Hypercare effort and post-deployment support continue beyond the SOW end date without a formal contract amendment.
riskDescription.consequence: The project may incur unbillable effort, eroding margin, and creating commercial and legal exposure due to work performed outside the contracted SOW period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Formalize SOW amendment or interim contractual arrangement immediately, documenting all post-August 31 effort, costs, and commercial terms with Premera approval.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon SOW amendment delay exceeding 10 business days, escalate to Ascendion legal and Premera executive sponsor for commercial resolution within 48 hours.
risks.reasoning: The SOW end date has already passed by 53 days with no amendment shown. Impact is High because unbillable effort and commercial exposure are material risks in a fixed-bid contract.

riskDescription.context: The original Go LIVE milestone was scheduled for July 1-15, 2026, but Production deployment was completed by October 23, 2026, indicating approximately 3 months of schedule slippage. (ART - Work Assignment; ALT - Watchlist Summary)
riskDescription.condition: If the mass producer onboarding planned for October 22, 2026 encounters technical or process issues.
riskDescription.consequence: The rollout may need to be rolled back and remediated, further delaying full production release and extending the already overrun SOW period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct phased producer onboarding starting with 100-user pilot cohort, validate end-to-end registration and authentication workflows before scaling to remaining 2,400+ producers.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If critical defects surface during onboarding, activate rollback procedure within 4 hours, redirect producers to legacy portal, and deploy hotfix within 24 hours.
risks.reasoning: End-to-end registration was validated with only 11 users before the big-bang rollout to 2,500+ producers, leaving limited evidence of production readiness at scale. Impact is High because rollback would extend the SOW overrun and delay business value realization.

riskDescription.context: 19 scope changes have been absorbed as of July 22, 2026, equivalent to 0.75-1 sprint of effort, and an open scope-change risk notes that further additions are likely. (ART - WSR; EMS - Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If additional scope changes are accepted without formal impact assessment and change control approval.
riskDescription.consequence: Another 0.5-1 sprint of unplanned effort may be absorbed, compressing remaining Hypercare activities and increasing the risk of quality compromise or further schedule slippage.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement change control board with Premera, requiring impact assessment and written approval for all scope changes during Hypercare, freezing scope after November 15, 2026.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If scope change exceeds 0.25 sprint effort, escalate to Premera Product Owner for prioritization against existing Hypercare backlog and defer non-critical items to Phase 2.
risks.reasoning: The scope-change risk has been open since June 29, 2026 with no mitigation plan defined, and the change rate has risen. Impact is Medium because the effort is recoverable but may compress Hypercare.

riskDescription.context: Actual effort is 8.0 against a baseline of 45.0 (about 82% below), and the team was formed on May 22, 2026, 2.5 months after the project start date of March 1, 2026. (EMS - Resources; EMS - Project Details)
riskDescription.condition: If effort remains well below baseline as post-deployment support and Hypercare activities ramp up.
riskDescription.consequence: The team may lack sufficient capacity to address production issues, support mass producer onboarding, and complete Hypercare activities, increasing the risk of service disruption or extended support period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Allocate two additional support engineers from Ascendion bench to Hypercare team by November 10, 2026, targeting 80% of baseline effort capacity within two weeks.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If production incidents exceed team capacity, engage Ascendion practice team for 24-hour surge support and communicate SLA impact to Premera within 2 hours.
risks.reasoning: Effort has remained far below baseline with no recovery shown, and the project is now in a critical post-deployment phase requiring rapid response to production issues. Impact is Medium because capacity shortfalls could delay issue resolution but are unlikely to cause full service failure.

riskDescription.context: No Business Analyst is assigned to the project, and only 2 Ascenders cover Scrum Master, Architect, Development, Functional Testing, and Regression Testing roles. (EMS - Resources)
riskDescription.condition: If either of the two Ascenders becomes unavailable due to attrition, extended leave, or reassignment during the post-deployment and Hypercare phase.
riskDescription.consequence: Critical knowledge and execution capacity may be lost, delaying issue resolution, support activities, and knowledge transfer, and increasing the risk of service disruption during mass producer onboarding.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Cross-train one non-Ascender team member on architecture and testing workflows by November 15, 2026, document all critical procedures in Confluence knowledge base.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon Ascender unavailability exceeding 3 business days, activate backup senior engineer from Ascendion practice team and initiate knowledge transfer within 24 hours.
risks.reasoning: Only 2 Ascenders cover 5 critical roles, creating concentration risk. Impact is High because loss of either Ascender during the critical post-deployment phase could severely impact service continuity.

riskDescription.context: Backend code coverage is 57% as of PI4 Sprint 3, compared to 98% for the frontend, and 86 CVEs were detected (4 critical, 82 high) on the alpine base image. (ART - WSR)
riskDescription.condition: If production workload or mass producer onboarding exposes untested backend code paths or exploits unpatched CVEs.
riskDescription.consequence: Defects or security vulnerabilities may surface in production, causing service disruption, data exposure, or compliance issues during the critical onboarding period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Increase backend unit test coverage to 75% by November 20, 2026, patch all critical and high CVEs using updated alpine base image before November 15.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If production defect or security incident occurs, activate incident response team within 1 hour, isolate affected service, and deploy emergency patch within 4 hours.
risks.reasoning: Backend code coverage is 41 percentage points below frontend, and 86 CVEs (including 4 critical) remain unresolved. Impact is High because production defects or security incidents during mass onboarding could cause service disruption or compliance exposure.

riskDescription.context: The Auth0 DB connection configuration update required for the ACPT environment move depends on one person (Drew) who holds access, and the dependency was flagged with an ETA of July 10, 2026. (ART - WSR)
riskDescription.condition: If Drew is unavailable when configuration updates or troubleshooting are needed during post-deployment support or mass producer onboarding.
riskDescription.consequence: Environment configuration issues may remain unresolved, delaying issue remediation or rollback actions and extending service disruption during the critical onboarding period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Request Premera to grant Auth0 configuration access to one Ascendion backup engineer by November 12, 2026, document all configuration procedures in runbook.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If Drew is unavailable and Auth0 issue arises, escalate to Premera Cyber team for emergency access provisioning within 2 hours and expedite configuration change.
risks.reasoning: No backup is documented for the Auth0 configuration access, but the dependency ETA has passed with no evidence of ongoing delay. Impact is Medium because configuration delays could extend issue resolution time but are unlikely to cause full service failure.

riskDescription.context: The scope-change risk was opened on June 29, 2026 with mitigation status 'Assessed' but no mitigation plan defined, and as of October 23, 2026 the risk is 116 days old with no mitigation. (EMS - Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If the open scope-change risk remains unmitigated and further scope additions are accepted during post-deployment support or Hypercare.
riskDescription.consequence: Uncontrolled scope growth may continue, consuming capacity needed for production support and extending the SOW overrun, with no mechanism to assess or approve the commercial and schedule impact.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Close Risk 857 by November 8, 2026, documenting all 19 absorbed scope changes, their effort impact, and implementing change control board for future requests.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If scope change request arrives without change control approval, reject request and escalate to Premera Product Owner for formal impact assessment and prioritization decision.
risks.reasoning: The risk has been open for 116 days with no mitigation plan, and the project is now in a phase where scope control is critical to manage SOW overrun. Impact is Medium because uncontrolled scope growth could extend the overrun but is unlikely to cause project failure.

riskDescription.context: Seven AAVA-related risks (single LLM limitations, tools integration delays, agent hardening, agent learning, client template alignment, tool/API invocation failures, agent orchestration) were opened between March 9-17, 2026 with no closure dates or ETAs stated. (ART - WSR)
riskDescription.condition: If AAVA agent limitations or integration issues surface during production workload or mass producer onboarding.
riskDescription.consequence: Agent-generated outputs may be inconsistent or incorrect, requiring manual intervention and increasing support effort during the critical onboarding period.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Document manual workflow paths for all AAVA-assisted tasks by November 18, 2026, ensuring team can operate without AAVA if agent issues arise during Hypercare.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If AAVA agent failure impacts production support, switch to manual workflow immediately, log all agent issues, and engage AAVA platform team for resolution within 24 hours.
risks.reasoning: AAVA-related risks have been open for 6-7 months with no closure, suggesting persistent issues. Impact is Medium because agent issues would increase support effort but the Work Assignment states AAVA is not required for the Deliverables to function post-Term.

riskDescription.context: Overall project progress remained at 19% from June 30 to July 15, 2026, indicating no measurable progress over a 15-day period, despite sprint velocity increasing from 49 to 88 story points. (ART - WSR)
riskDescription.condition: If the disconnect between sprint velocity and overall progress persists during post-deployment support and Hypercare.
riskDescription.consequence: Actual project completion and knowledge transfer activities may be delayed beyond the planned project end date of December 31, 2026, extending resource commitment and cost.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Align milestone tracking with sprint completion by November 25, 2026, updating EMS milestones to reflect Production deployment and Hypercare progress weekly.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If milestone tracking disconnect continues, escalate to Ascendion PMO for EMS audit and synchronization, ensuring accurate project status reporting to Premera by December 2.
risks.reasoning: The progress stall occurred during the Build phase, and Production deployment has since been completed. Impact is Low because the project is now in post-deployment support, and the disconnect is primarily a tracking issue rather than a delivery blocker.
